'''Lisa-ann Gershwin''', also known as '''Lisa Gershwin''', is an American-Australian biologist based in [[Launceston, Tasmania|Launceston]], [[Tasmania]], who has described over 200 species of [[jellyfish]],<ref name="Mather">{{cite web |url=http://www.themercury.com.au/news/tasmania/expert-in-deadly-jellyfish-loses-job-as-funds-dry-up/story-fnj4f7k1-1226970088102 |title=Expert in deadly jellyfish loses job as funds dry up |last=Mather |first=Annie |date=29 June 2014 |work=Hobart Mercury |publisher=News Ltd |access-date=20 January 2015}}</ref> and written and co-authored several non-fiction books about [[Cnidaria]] (jellyfish and allies) including ''Stung!'' (2013) and ''Jellyfish – A Natural History'' (2016). She provides independent advice related to jellyfish worldwide to the media, online and via The Jellyfish App.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://thejellyfishapp.com/|title=The Jellyfish App|website=thejellyfishapp.com|language=en|access-date=2019-12-23}}</ref> She was an unsuccessful candidate in the [[2021 Tasmanian state election]] running as an independent in the [[Division of Clark (state)|electorate of Clark]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Home - lisagershwin.com|url=https://lisagershwin.com/|access-date=2021-05-01|website=lisagershwin.com|language=en}}</ref>

== Education ==
Born in [[Los Angeles]], [[California]],{{citation needed|date=April 2025}} Gershwin began studying jellyfish in 1992.

In 1993, she received an Associate of Arts degree in biology from [[Los Angeles Pierce College]].<ref name="CV"/>

In 1997, Gershwin was awarded a Bachelor of Science in [[Marine Biology]] from [[California State University Northridge]].<ref name="CV"/>

She was a [[Fulbright Program|Fulbright Fellow]] in 1998–1999.{{citation needed|date=April 2025}}

Gershwin earned a Ph.D. in [[Integrative Biology]] from the [[University of California Berkeley]] in 2003 and completed a second Ph.D. in Marine Biology at [[James Cook University]] in 2005.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://people.csiro.au/G/L/Lisa-Ann-Gershwin|title=Dr Lisa Gershwin|website=people.csiro.au|language=en|access-date=2017-02-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180425093317/http://people.csiro.au/G/L/Lisa-Ann-Gershwin|archive-date=2018-04-25|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="CV">[http://www.stingeradvisor.com/CV.htm "CV: Lisa-Ann Gershwin"], ''stingeradvisor.com''. Accessed June 30, 2020.</ref>

== Career ==
Gershwin has worked with and for a range of scientific organisations, including [[Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation|CSIRO]]<ref name=":1" /> from circa 2012 to early 2019.<ref name=":2" />

She developed a system to predict blooms of the hazardous [[Irukandji jellyfish]] in [[north Queensland]]. She led a team that discovered that the blooms coincide with the blooming of [[salp]]s, and that these were prompted by [[upwelling]] after the dying down of [[trade wind]]s.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blog.csiro.au/improving-prediction-of-deadly-irukandji-jellyfish-blooms/ |title=Improving prediction of deadly Irukandji jellyfish blooms|last=Kachel |first=Nicholas |date=14 May 2014 |work=News@CSIRO|publisher=CSIRO|access-date=20 October 2016}}</ref> In December 2017 Gershwin's team refined a model for the early warning forecasting systems for irukandjis, with water testing off [[Cairns]]' northern beaches.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.cairnspost.com.au/business/scientists-hope-for-jellyfish-bloom-in-waters-off-cairns/news-story/e0de789eb5f5797f704d20d82ef14fdc|title=Science's sting in tail|access-date=2018-01-02|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.cairnspost.com.au/business/scientists-developing-early-warning-and-early-detection-for-irukandji/news-story/03b12a34587041aea2f351aecf145e70|title=Subscribe to the Cairns Post|website=www.cairnspost.com.au|language=en|access-date=2018-01-02}}</ref>

She has described several venomous jellyfish—nine species of irukandji,<ref name="Science Show" /> including the Queensland species ''[[Malo kingi]]'' and ''[[Malo maxima]]'',<ref>Gershwin, L. (2007). [http://www.mapress.com/zootaxa/2007f/z01659p068f.pdf ''Malo kingi'': A new species of Irukandji jellyfish (Cnidaria: Cubozoa: Carybdeida), possibly lethal to humans, from Queensland, Australia.] ''Zootaxa'' 1659 55–68.</ref> and the giant irukandji species ''[[Keesingia gigas]]'' from Western Australia, which was discovered without tentacles.<ref>{{cite news|title=New toxic jellyfish with no tentacles found in WA|url=http://www.australiangeographic.com.au/news/2014/08/new-jellyfish-species-with-no-tentacles-found-in-wa|access-date=17 November 2014|website=Australian Geographic|date=8 August 2014}}</ref>
[[File:Bazinga rieki2.JPG|alt=Image of Bazinga rieki, described and photographed by Geshwin|thumb|Bazinga rieki, described and photographed by Geshwin]]
Gershwin was one of the co-describers of the unusual jellyfish ''[[Bazinga rieki]]'', which is the sole member of the new family Bazingidae and partly named for the colloquialism uttered by Dr. [[Sheldon Cooper]] in the TV program ''[[The Big Bang Theory]]''.<ref name=GershwinDavie>{{cite journal|url=http://www.qm.qld.gov.au/~/media/Documents/QM/About%20Us/Publications/Memoirs%20-%20Nature/N56-2/qmn56-2-gershwin-davie.pdf|author1=Gershwin, L.  |author2=Davie, P.J.F. |name-list-style=amp|date=30 June 2013|title=A remarkable new jellyfish (Cnidaria: Scyphozoa) from coastal Australia, representing a new suborder within the Rhizostomeae. Memoirs of the Queensland Museum — ''Nature'' 56(2)|journal=Proceedings of the ... International Congress of Arachnology |pages=625–630|publisher=Queensland Museum|doi=10.17082/j.2204-1478.56.2.2013-18 |issn=0079-8835 }}</ref> In early 2014, a giant "snotty" jellyfish some 1.5m in diameter was discovered at a beach in [[Howden, Tasmania|Howden]], south of [[Hobart]]. Studied by Gershwin currently, it is due to be described in a future paper.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Levy|first=Megan|date=February 6, 2014|title=New species of giant 'snotty' jellyfish found in Tasmania|journal=Sydney Morning Herald|publisher= Fairfax Media|url=http://www.smh.com.au/environment/animals/new-species-of-giant-snotty-jellyfish-found-in-tasmania-20140206-323ko.html}}</ref> In 2015, Gershwin was preparing to name three undescribed species with input from visitors to the celebrations for CSIRO's new research vessel.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Mounster |first=Bruce |date=8 January 2015 |title=Shaping up as big year for jellyfish in southern Tasmanian waters |url=https://www.themercury.com.au/news/tasmania/shaping-up-as-big-year-for-jellyfish-in-southern-tasmanian-waters/news-story/2f7f9dd495904eeeedb97ce6b3c91b3d |access-date=2 August 2024 |work=Mercury}}</ref>

Gershwin was named one of the Top 100 Australian Scientists by the Science Show in 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-10-21 |title=Against the current: Dr Lisa-Ann Gershwin’s path to science {{!}} Royal Society |url=https://royalsociety.org/blog/2024/12/lisa-ann-gershwin/ |access-date=2026-10-26 |website=royalsociety.org |language=en}}</ref>

== Publications ==

=== Books ===
Gershwin's 2013 book entitled ''Stung'' describes the diversity and adaptability of jellyfish, and their increasing numbers at the expense of other organisms worldwide, through [[Overfishing|over-fishing]], [[pollution]] and modification of the marine environment. She concedes there is little that can be done to reverse or even halt the process of the marine environment becoming dominated by jellyfish worldwide.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.nybooks.com/articles/archives/2013/sep/26/jellyfish-theyre-taking-over/|title=They're Taking Over!|last=Flannery|first=Tim|date=26 September 2013|magazine=The New York Review of Books|publisher=NYREV|access-date=20 January 2015}}</ref>

In 2016, Gershwin's 224 page book ''Jellyfish – a natural history'' was published by The Ivy Press. It covers jellyfish anatomy, life history, taxonomy and ecology and includes species level information and many full page photographs.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://bookshop.nla.gov.au/book/jellyfish-a-natural-history.do|title=National Library of Australia Bookshop|website=bookshop.nla.gov.au|language=en|access-date=2017-02-17}}</ref>

In 2023, Gershwin's book, ''Shapeshifters: The Wondrous World of Jellyfish'', was published by Abrams.

=== Articles ===
Gershwin wrote for [[The Conversation (website)|The Conversation]] in December 2015 about blue bottles,<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://theconversation.com/the-blue-bottles-are-coming-but-what-exactly-are-these-creatures-48675|title=The blue bottles are coming, but what exactly are these creatures?|last=Gershwin|first=Lisa-ann|work=The Conversation|access-date=2017-11-12|language=en}}</ref> and in January 2016, about deadly sea creatures.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://theconversation.com/dont-go-in-the-water-a-world-of-pain-awaits-in-australias-deep-blue-seas-50844|title=Don't go in the water: a world of pain awaits in Australia's deep blue seas|last=Gershwin|first=Lisa-ann|work=The Conversation|access-date=2017-11-12|language=en}}</ref>

In November 2017, Gershwin completed an invited book review for [[Nature (journal)|Nature]], spanning [[Juli Berwald]]'s ''Spineless: the science of jellyfish and the art of growing a backbone'', and Danna Staaf's ''Squid empire: the rise and fall of the cephalopods''.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Gershwin|first=Lisa-ann|date=2 November 2017|title=Zoology: The joys of spinelessness|journal=Nature|volume= 551| issue =  32|page=32|doi=10.1038/551032a|bibcode=2017Natur.551...32G|doi-access=free}}</ref>

===Profiles and news interviews ===

==== Profiles ====
In February 2014, Gershwin was interviewed by Bec Crew for [[Scientific American]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://blogs.scientificamerican.com/running-ponies/in-conversation-with-lisa-anne-gershwin-jellyfish-savant/|title=In Conversation with Lisa-Anne Gershwin, Jellyfish Savant|last=Crew|first=Bec|work=Scientific American Blog Network|access-date=2017-11-12|language=en}}</ref>

In June 2014, Gershwin was highlighted as a valuable expert in Anne Mather's article on funding cuts for CSIRO's Hobart office.<ref name="Mather" /> In January 2019, ABC reported that Gershwin's role at CSIRO would finish in February as her contract was not being renewed, but that she would continue her jellyfish research through her private consultancy.<ref name=":2">{{Cite news|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2019-01-10/jellyfish-expert-employment-ends-with-csiro/10701400|title=Irukandji warning system in doubt as leading stinger expert departs CSIRO|last=Sundstrom|first=Kathy|date=10 January 2019|work=ABC news|access-date=24 April 2019}}</ref>

In May 2017, Gershwin was interviewed by [[Richard Fidler]] for ABC Radio.<ref>{{Citation|title=The delicate and deadly world of jellyfish: from Bazinga to Shiraz|date=2017-04-26|url=http://www.abc.net.au/radio/programs/conversations/conversations-lisa-gershwin/8471360|publisher=Australian Broadcasting Corporation|language=en-AU|access-date=2018-01-04}}</ref>

==== News interviews ====
In February 2017, Gershwin commented on a [[jellyfish bloom]] at [[Deception Bay, Queensland|Deception Bay]], as being the biggest she had seen in her 25 years of research.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.abc.net.au/news/2017-02-02/wallpaper-of-jellyfish-wash-up-on-queensland-beach/8234454|title=Thousands of jellyfish wash up on Queensland beach|date=2017-02-02|work=ABC News|access-date=2018-01-04|language=en-AU}}</ref> In January 2018, she was interviewed about an unusual wave of bluebottles in Cairns.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.heraldsun.com.au/news/national/northern-beaches-awash-with-bluebottles/news-story/b315c4ba07ef50f9cd4a211287679bff|title=Northern Beaches awash with bluebottles|last=Bateman|first=Daniel|date=4 January 2018|work=The Cairns Post|access-date=4 January 2018|url-access=subscription }}</ref> In January 2018, the [[The Atlantic|Atlantic]] cited her 2007 Radio National interview on the symptoms of being stung by irukandji, Malo kingi.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theatlantic.com/magazine/archive/2018/01/listening-to-jellyfish/546542/|title=Imagining the Jellyfish Apocalypse|last=Giggs|first=Rebecca|work=The Atlantic|access-date=2018-01-04|language=en-US}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Gershwin is related to composer [[George Gershwin]].<ref name="Science Show">{{cite web|url=http://www.abc.net.au/radionational/programs/scienceshow/gershwin--the-irukandji/3424048#transcript|title=Gershwin & the Irukandji|last=Williams|first=Robyn|date=17 July 2004|work=The Science Show|publisher=Australian Broadcasting Corporation (ABC)|access-date=24 January 2015}}</ref> She was diagnosed with [[Asperger syndrome]] in 2010.<ref>{{cite web|title=A Scientist with Heart. About me|website=Dr Lisa-ann Gershwin (lisagershwin.com)|url=http://lisagershwin.com/about}}</ref>
